papers.title: The series of genetic codes that preceded our own.
papers.abstract: We produce a working hypothesis for the steps by which the canonical genetic code might have been constructed. We assume amino acids were added in the order inferred from their enrichment or depletion in ancestrally reconstructed sequences dating back to the Last Universal Common Ancestor (LUCA) relative to that in ancient but post-LUCA controls. To convert this ordering into a time series of 64-codon genetic codes, we followed the "2-1-3 rule" that information appeared first at the middle codon position, then mostly at the first before the third, with purine vs pyrimidine distinctions tending to precede distinctions between purines or between pyrimidines. Two notable deviations from the 2-1-3 rule suggest an ancestral promiscuity between valine/isoleucine/methionine, and between alanine/threonine, to produce "statistical proteins." The same promiscuities enable amino acids to be added in order of appearance at successive nodes in the cladograms of Class I and Class II aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase catalytic domains. Trifonov's previous amino acid ordering did not produce this consilience, with both a worse fit to the 2-1-3 rule, and discordance of synthetase trees with the order. More support for late resolution of hydrophobic promiscuity comes from post-LUCA differentiation between the synthetases of valine and isoleucine, in a manner dependent on 2 conserved tryptophans. The observed promiscuous activities of synthetases, and deep mutational scanning data on which amino acid substitutions are best tolerated, also align well with our reconstructed time series of genetic codes. As a working hypothesis, this series can guide research on random peptides, urzymes, and substitution models.

papers.title: Identification and dating of pregnancies in administrative healthcare claims databases: An updated, transparent, and transportable algorithm.
papers.abstract: Studies using routinely collected healthcare data are essential for understanding the benefit-risk profile of medications in pregnancy. However, reproducibility is limited by the lack of shared pregnancy identification algorithms, and generalizability is constrained by their development primarily in commercial insurance databases. A previously developed pregnancy identification algorithm was updated for ICD-10-CM and translated into a standardized format to support transport across diverse databases. Algorithm implementation characteristics were evaluated in three US health insurance claims databases (2000-2025), including commercially and publicly insured populations. Overall, 5.8 million and 3.0 million pregnancies were identified in two commercial databases (Merative™ and Optum) and 2.3 million pregnancies in Merative™ MarketScan® Multi-State Medicaid Database (MDCD). Across databases, live birth prevalence ranged from 76-83%, miscarriage/abortion 15-23%, ectopic pregnancy 1%, and stillbirth ≤0.5%, with a higher proportion of live births in MDCD. Pregnancy dating methods varied substantially across coding eras: use of gestational age records increased from 4-9% in the ICD-9-CM era to 87-92% during the ICD-10-CM era, with greater use in MDCD. Using a standardized algorithm, this study demonstrates how database characteristics and coding transitions influence pregnancy identification and dating in healthcare data, highlighting methodological considerations for reproducible pregnancy research across data sources.

papers.title: Psychosocial predictors of treatment adherence and quality of life among patients with uveitis in a tertiary care hospital, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess the prevalence of treatment adherence and quality of life among patients with uveitis, and to examine the influence of psychosocial predictors including depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms and adult attachment style on these outcomes. METHODS: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted at the uveitis outpatient clinics in King Saud University Medical City in Riyadh between December 2024 and July 2025. Adult patients aged 18 years or older with a confirmed diagnosis of uveitis were eligible for inclusion. Patients completed a self-administered Arabic electronic questionnaire including validated instruments: the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) for anxiety, Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) for depression, Visual Function Index-14 (VF-14) for quality of life, Modified Experiences in Close Relationships Scale (ECR-M16) for attachment style, and a Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for medication adherence. RESULTS: Among the 248 participants, 199 (80.2%) were adherent to treatment. A significant association was observed between non-adherence to medication and depression (p = 0.041). Depression and anxiety were identified in 27% and 23.8% of participants, respectively. The median VF-14 score was 92.9 (IQR: 77.3-98.2). 22.6% attributed uveitis to psychological stress and 16.1% to supernatural causes like the evil eye, magic or jinn possession, and 34.3% used ruqyah (faith healing) as a treatment. In bivariate analysis, age, educational level, marital status, employment, anxiety and depression were significantly associated with quality of life. In the multivariable model, only university education (β = 13.09, 95% CI: 4.25-21.93; p = 0.004) and depression (β = -8.58, 95% CI: -13.83 to -3.33; p = 0.001) remained independently associated with quality of life. papers.title: Identification and Validation of Hub Genes Associated With Periodontitis and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accumulating evidence suggests a close relationship between periodontitis and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE); however, the shared molecular mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate genes and molecular features shared between periodontitis and SLE through integrative bioinformatics analysis and clinical validation. METHODS: Gene expression profiles were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database, and differentially expressed genes (DEGs) shared between periodontitis and SLE were identified. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses were performed, followed by protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction and hub gene screening. The expression patterns of the hub genes were evaluated in independent validation datasets, and their discriminatory performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Immune cell infiltration and its correlations with hub gene expression were further investigated. Transcription factor-microRNA regulatory networks and candidate compounds were computationally predicted. Finally, quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) was performed to validate hub gene expression in clinical samples. RESULTS: A total of 124 overlapping DEGs were identified, from which five hub genes-CCL3, LY96, FOS, MMP9, and PTGS2-were selected. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses indicated that the overlapping DEGs were predominantly associated with inflammatory and immune-related biological processes and signaling pathways. All five hub genes showed consistent expression patterns in the independent periodontitis validation dataset, whereas FOS, LY96, and PTGS2, but not CCL3 and MMP9, showed consistent differential expression in the independent SLE validation dataset. papers.title: Enhancing relationship quality in couples affected by ADHD: a randomized controlled study of a couple's intervention.
papers.abstract: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is highly prevalent among adults, making it one of the most common psychiatric diagnoses in this population associated with negative functional impact across multiple life areas, including romantic relationships. Despite this, scientifically evaluated interventions specifically targeting relationship quality in couples where one or both partners have ADHD remain limited. This study presents a randomized controlled evaluation of a couple-based intervention for ADHD, assessing its impact on relationship quality and participants' experiences. Eighty couples (n = 160 participants) were randomized to either an intervention group or a waitlist control group, with assessments conducted at baseline, post-intervention, and three-month follow-up. Intention-to-treat analyses using Linear Mixed Models indicated no significant between-group difference for the primary outcome of relationship quality (QDR-36), nor for secondary outcomes of stress, depression, anxiety, or ADHD-related quality of life. A significant between-group interaction effect was found for ADHD symptoms (ASRS), however, this effect unexpectedly favored the waitlist control group, which showed a greater reduction in symptoms compared to the intervention group. The participants' evaluation of the course indicated an overall high rating of satisfaction with the content. Suggestions for improving access to the course as well as improving the course's effect on relationship quality are discussed.

papers.title: Negative Partner Perceptions as an Indirect Pathway Between Critical Adverse Experiences and Negative Communication in Adult Romantic Relationships.
papers.journal: Journal of marital and family therapy
papers.abstract: Adverse experiences, distressing or harmful lived events, affect multiple domains of functioning and are consistently linked to poorer relational functioning. However, cognitive mechanisms linking adverse experiences to communication behaviors in romantic relationships remain understudied. "Critical" adverse experiences (CAEs) involving interpersonal harm or mental health concerns may be especially impactful. Drawing on cognitive and stress-based frameworks, this study examined whether CAEs were indirectly associated with negative conflict behaviors through negative partner perceptions. Self-report data from 2814 individuals across three waves of the German Family Panel were analyzed using longitudinal structural equation modeling. Greater exposure to CAEs was associated with more negative partner perceptions, which in turn predicted subsequent negative communication behaviors. The indirect effect was significant but small, supporting a temporally ordered cognitive pathway. Findings extend cross-sectional research by demonstrating three-wave longitudinal associations and highlight the impact of CAEs across the lifespan. Implications for clinicians and researchers are discussed.

papers.title: Ecological and social cues orchestrate concerted courtship in Drosophila.
papers.abstract: Mating decisions are often attributed to the sensory signalling between prospective sexual partners. Yet these interactions are also shaped by the broader environmental context in which they unfold, to appropriately align sexual arousal with reproductive opportunities1-6. Here we show that in Drosophila erecta mating is strictly contingent on the ecological and social environment generated as flies densely aggregate in groups on a food patch. We find that food volatiles directly promote male sexual arousal, triggering individuals to sample and pursue potential mates, giving rise to dynamic interactions across the group. The ensuing visual motion transforms each male's visual field, which in turn further amplifies his arousal, generating a multisensory feedback loop that coordinately promotes courtship across individuals. D. erecta's strict dependence on environmental cues appears latent in related species, such as Drosophila melanogaster, where food odour can promote arousal7 but is dispensable for vigorous courtship. Comparative circuit analyses show that species-specific thresholds for sexual arousal reflect variation in how olfactory input modulates conserved nodes controlling courtship drive, rendering food volatiles a strict sensory gate only in D. erecta. Together, our findings highlight how environmental cues not directly tied to sexual signalling can profoundly influence reproductive behaviour and reorganize the social landscape to ensure mating occurs in contexts where reproductive opportunities are abundant.

papers.title: "Living in the shadow of treatment": Drug rehabilitation and life-course experiences of ethnic minority youth in Southwest China.
papers.journal: The International journal on drug policy
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: China's drug rehabilitation system has begun to receive increasing research attention. This emerging research tends to treat institutional treatment, community rehabilitation, and post-treatment experiences as separate stages. However, the experiences of ethnic minority young people in this system remain under-researched. This study examines how ethnic minority youth in Southwest China experience compulsory isolation and community-based drug rehabilitation across the life course, with particular attention to what participants described as the enduring "shadows" of treatment. METHODS: Drawing on a multi-site ethnographic study, which includes in-depth interviews with 17 ethnic minority youth who had experienced compulsory isolation rehabilitation and community-based rehabilitation, the study combines thematic coding with a life-course analysis. This approach enables us to trace how treatment is narrated across periods before, during and after formal institutional intervention. RESULTS: The findings show that treatment casts a shadow across three connected temporal moments. Before entering treatment, participants described it through peers' stories, "luck-seeking" optimism and distrust toward rehabilitation institutions. During treatment, compulsory isolation and community-based rehabilitation were experienced as forceful interventions that reorganised everyday life through confinement, discipline, moral correction and surveillance. After treatment, rehabilitation histories continued to shape employment opportunities, intimate relationships, family life and community belonging, while some participants sought alternative forms of healing through local ritual and Buddhist practices. CONCLUSION: The findings show how stigma and claims to care extended the rehabilitation system beyond the formal period of treatment, remaining embedded in participants' social relationships and life trajectories. papers.title: Genetic analysis of 7,000 year old preserved goat leather from Cueva de los Murciélagos (Albuñol, Spain).
papers.abstract: Advances in ancient DNA research have expanded the range of materials from which genetic information can be recovered, enabling the analysis of atypical materials. These often preserve both host and exogenous DNA, for example due to handling or native microbes, offering a window into past diversity. Here we report one such exceptional material: a well-preserved goat leather specimen from Cueva de los Murciélagos (Albuñol, Spain), associated with an Early Neolithic context. Archaeozoological analyses show clear evidence of tanning and anthropogenic modification of the skin, while radiocarbon dating confirms it to be ~ 7,250-7,000 years old. We generated genome-wide data from the leather (Murciélagos1) and demonstrated that it derives from a domestic goat of European ancestry. Comparisons with modern goats show highest affinity to the Bermeya breed from northern Spain, demonstrating genetic connectivity in goat herds from the Neolithic to present day Iberia. We additionally recover fragmented DNA from the leather deriving from human and canid sources, the former likely reflecting handling/wearing of the leather and the latter indicating post-depositional disturbance. Murciélagos1 represents one of the oldest nuclear genome data from organic remains outside of high altitude, high latitude regions, and demonstrates the value of ancient DNA analysis in exceptional cases of organic preservation.

papers.title: Poised for Allostery: Specific Interactions Underlie Precise Positioning of the C-Terminal Tail in Phosphofructokinase-1.
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.abstract: Disordered terminal segments often regulate enzymes, but how such flexible elements achieve the spatial precision required for allostery remains poorly understood. Using human phosphofructokinase-1 as a model system, we combine enhanced-sampling molecular dynamics simulations, conservation-guided spatial analysis, prior allosteric network analysis, and coarse-grained modeling to show that allosteric positioning of the C-terminal tail, defined by residue-level contacts with the catalytic and regulatory domains, is maintained by a few key hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions. This positioning enables the conserved tail residues L766 and E767 to dynamically couple the tail to the active site through a conserved surface region and to bridge the catalytic and regulatory domains in the T-state, experimentally associated with ATP inhibition. In contrast, coarse-grained simulations lacking explicit directional representation of hydrogen-bonding interactions fail to maintain stable tail docking, whereas including selected OLIVES-derived native hydrogen-bond terms improves the stability of the T-state-like docking pose. These findings support sequence-specific surface docking of a disordered enzyme tail as a physicochemical mechanism for allosteric regulation.

papers.title: Dissociative Electron Attachment in 1,3-Dimethyl-5-Thiocyanatouracil at Different Hydration Conditions.
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.abstract: 5-Thiocyanato-2'-deoxyuridine has emerged as a promising radiosensitizer for cancer radiotherapy. Upon X-ray irradiation, hydrated electrons generated in the tumor microenvironment can interact with this molecule, forming reactive transient species capable of inducing damage to DNA, the primary target of radiotherapy. In this work, we investigate dissociative electron attachment (DEA) to 1,3-dimethyl-5-thiocyanatouracil, a doubly methylated analogue of 5-thiocyanato-2'-deoxyuridine, in both the gas phase and microhydrated environments. Gas-phase measurements were performed using a crossed electron-molecular beam apparatus coupled with mass spectrometry, while microhydrated clusters were examined using a CLUster-Beam setup, enabling direct assessment of hydration effects on DEA. The experimental results are supported by quantum chemical calculations, providing insight into thermodynamic and kinetic parameters, including electron affinities, reaction thresholds, and activation barriers. In both environments, the parent anion and the CN- fragment dominate the product distribution, accompanied by minor channels such as SCN- formation. Microhydration leads to a moderate suppression of the S-CN bond cleavage pathway but does not inhibit the reaction. Overall, these findings demonstrate that microhydration modulates, yet preserves, DEA activity in this class of radiosensitizers, supporting their potential effectiveness under biologically relevant conditions.

papers.title: Smallest Endohedral Water Cage Featuring a Nonclassic Polyhedron: Experimental Observation of (H2O)17.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: The structural transition from clustered water molecules to the hydrogen-bonding networks of bulk liquid defines one of the most fundamental problems in physical chemistry, yet the precise size at which the endohedral cages emerge remains experimentally elusive. While theory has long predicted that a fully encapsulated water molecule requires a minimum of 16-23 surrounding molecules, direct experimental identification has been hindered by the difficulty of size selection of neutral clusters. Using infrared spectroscopy coupled to vacuum-ultraviolet threshold photoionization, we provide the first experimental evidence that (H2O)17 forms the smallest water endohedral cage, achieving a decades-standing goal of establishing the molecular limit of a solvation shell. Surprisingly, the oxygen framework of this (H2O)17 cage defines an unprecedented, nonclassic polyhedron with four tetragonal, four pentagonal, and two hexagonal faces that breaks the symmetry constraints of all classical Platonic, Archimedean, and Johnson solids. This work establishes a critical structural precursor to the hydrogen-bonding network topology observed in condensed-phase water and offers new perspectives at the multidisciplinary sciences of mathematics, materials, physics, and chemistry.

papers.title: Control of Sequences and H-Bonding Motifs in IEM-Derived Copolymers Enables Mechanical Tunability, Self-Healing, and Clusterization-Triggered Emission.
papers.abstract: The chemical identity and spatial arrangement of hydrogen-bonding (H-bonding) motifs along a polymer chain influence mechanical property, but their coupled effects on stiffness, self-healing, and optical activity within a well-defined backbone remain largely unexplored. Here, we install single, double, and quadruple H-bonding motifs (including urethane, urea, aliphatic, and aromatic variants) into methyl methacrylate-co-butyl acrylate gradient copolymers (MMA-g-BA) via ATRP, using 2-isocyanatoethyl methacrylate (IEM) as a versatile reactive pendant side-chain handle. Systematic evaluation reveals that mechanical performance is governed by motif identity and chain architecture rather than H-bond density alone. Young's moduli span nearly two orders of magnitude (29-640 MPa), while the quadruple H-bonding gradient copolymer achieves an excellent balance of stiffness (∼262 MPa) and toughness (∼20 MJ m-3), together with efficient self-healing, recovering >90% of Young's modulus within 0.5 h and 80% of toughness after 3 h at 90°C. We further report, for the first time, clusterization-triggered emission (CTE) in the aliphatic MMA-g-BA matrix, with quadruple H-bonding motifs enhancing photoluminescence by promoting emissive cluster aggregation, evidenced by a lower critical cluster concentration than the unfunctionalized matrix. These findings establish motif selection and sequence control as coupled design parameters for simultaneously programming mechanical, self-healing, and photoluminescent properties in a single poly(acrylate/methacrylate) platform.

papers.title: Nectin-4 mediates rubella virus entry in airway and placental cells.
papers.abstract: Rubella virus (RuV) causes rubella and, when acquired during pregnancy, congenital rubella syndrome1. Despite its clinical significance, the cellular entry mechanism of RuV remains poorly characterized, owing to limited identification of host receptors2, which hinders pathogenesis research and therapeutic development. Here, using proximity biotin labelling-based proteomics coupled with CRISPR-Cas9 validation, we identify nectin-4 as a functional RuV entry receptor. Ectopic expression of nectin-4 conferred susceptibility to RuV in non-permissive cells, whereas blocking or genetic ablation of nectin-4 reduced infection, results that demonstrate that nectin-4 is a major entry factor. Mechanistically, nectin-4 directly interacts with the RuV envelope glycoprotein heterodimer and facilitates receptor-mediated endocytosis following initial calcium-dependent viral attachment to cellular lipids. In polarized airway epithelial models, nectin-4 mediates basolateral entry of RuV and supports apical progeny release, a finding that provides a molecular mechanism for respiratory transmission. In placental models, nectin-4 is highly expressed on syncytiotrophoblasts and facilitates infection at the maternal-fetal interface, although additional nectin-4-independent pathways contribute to infection of other trophoblast populations. Together, these data establish nectin-4 as a key factor for respiratory transmission and early placental infection of RuV and highlight it as a promising therapeutic target for the prevention of rubella and related diseases.

papers.title: Sub-nanomolar hydrogen peroxide detection via catalase direct electron transfer in a hierarchical sandwich-structured TiO2-carbon nanotube/cysteine-gold/nafion bioelectrode.
papers.journal: Analytical sciences : the international journal of the Japan Society for Analytical Chemistry
papers.abstract: Accurate trace-level H2O2 detection is critical across a wide range of fields, including biomedical, food, and industrial monitoring, yet a catalase-based platform combining a sub-nanomolar detection limit with high sensitivity, robust operational stability, and reproducibility remains a major unmet need and an area of strong demand. Herein, we present a third-generation H2O2 biosensor in which bovine liver catalase (CAT) is immobilized on a hierarchically engineered glassy carbon electrode (GCE), with a TiO2-carboxylated multiwalled carbon nanotube (TiO2-cMWCNTs) hybrid sandwiched between a cysteine-gold nanoparticle (Cys-AuNPs) anchoring layer and a thin Nafion (NF) permselective overlayer (NF/CAT/TiO₂-cMWCNTs/Cys-AuNPs/GCE). Characterization (TEM, SEM, SEM-EDS, FTIR) confirmed uniform TiO2 distribution and direct -COOH/TiO2 coupling, with carboxylate and hydrogen-bonding signatures indicating a chemically integrated network that provides an oxygen-rich, hydrophilic microenvironment, stabilizing CAT against subunit dissociation and activity loss while preserving a continuous, conductive direct electron-transfer (DET) pathway. Within this architecture H2O2 drives the turnover, the heme generates the analytical signal, and the surrounding layers anchor, host, wire, and shield the enzyme. Mechanistically, whereas catalase-based biosensors typically invoke the Compound I/Compound II cycle only schematically, we anchor this cycle, the H2O2-turnover mechanism of catalase that proceeds through two high-valent heme intermediates, in deposited crystal structures through a PDB-guided active-site analysis (bovine catalase 3RE8, cross-validated against 3NWL, with sub-ångström RMSD to the experimentally resolved Compound I (1MQF) and Compound II ferryl-hydroxo (2CAG) intermediates). papers.title: Individual, interpersonal, and socioeconomic predictors of divorce: A 12-year prospective study.
papers.journal: Journal of personality and social psychology
papers.abstract: Divorce is among the most common and costly life disruptions adults may face. Maladaptive and ineffective couple communication is routinely implicated in leading models as the cause of divorce, and interventions designed to prevent divorce accordingly prioritize changes in couple interaction patterns. Yet research linking couple communication to divorce has been inconsistent, and failures of communication-based interventions highlight the need for an expanded view of early signs of risk. Alternative perspectives on divorce draw attention to the vulnerabilities individuals bring into marriage and the socioeconomic circumstances couples must navigate once married, yet the predictive power of these perspectives has never been directly compared to the behavioral model. The current analyses address this gap through a study of 368 different-sex newlywed couples who provided data on six clusters of predictors within 6 months of marriage: relationship satisfaction for each spouse, individual vulnerabilities for each spouse, couples' adaptive behavior, and socioeconomic risk. Over the next 12 years, 39% of couples divorced. Preregistered Bayesian structural equation models and survival analyses demonstrated that each baseline risk factor independently predicted divorce in the expected direction. When all predictors were included simultaneously, only wives' individual vulnerabilities predicted divorce. Adaptive communication behaviors attenuated the risk conferred by wives' vulnerabilities. The best performing model explained 34% of variance in divorce, suggesting that at least one third of couples' divorce risk is detectable early in marriage. Exploring vulnerabilities and their effects promises to deepen understanding of how relationships develop and deteriorate and can clarify boundary conditions of behavioral models of divorce. papers.title: Association Between Help Seeking, Motivation, and Relationship Satisfaction in Couples Post Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.journal: Journal of marital and family therapy
papers.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) presents significant challenges for couples, affecting communication, emotional regulation, and overall relationship dynamics. This study examines the association between help-seeking, motivation, and relationship satisfaction in couples where one partner has experienced a TBI. Specifically, we investigated (a) how self-stigma for help-seeking influenced motivation for mental health service engagement in both partners and (b) whether these associations varied by relationship satisfaction. Using the actor partner interdependence model (APIM), we assessed 160 couples to explore the interdependence of help-seeking stigma on both motivation and perceived relationship quality. Results indicated that there was a statistically significant difference in perceived relationship quality between TBI and non-TBI partners. Actor and partner effects were not statistically significant in this sample. However, the findings highlight the complexities of relational dynamics in TBI-affected couples and emphasize the need for further research on TBI related help-seeking stigma and relational support mechanisms.

papers.title: Association Between Early Postpartum Maternal Fatigue and Infant Emotional Development: Protocol for a Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Postpartum fatigue (PPF) is clinically defined as persistent physical and mental exhaustion emerging after childbirth that cannot be fully relieved by rest. It is distinct from postpartum depression and has a prevalence of 76.13% among Chinese women within the first postpartum week. Existing evidence suggests that maternal PPF may alter salivary oxytocin concentrations, disturb maternal caregiving behaviors, and subsequently interfere with multiple dimensions of infant emotional development, including emotional expression, emotional regulation, and emotional recognition. Objective psychophysiological measurements, such as eye-tracking and galvanic skin response, have been validated for assessing infant emotional responses. Nevertheless, most existing studies focus merely on maternal mental well-being. Local longitudinal evidence clarifying this sequential mechanistic chain remains limited, and targeted early screening and intervention strategies for PPF-affected mother-infant dyads are insufficient. OBJECTIVE: This prospective cohort protocol aims to examine the independent association between maternal PPF and the emotional development of 3-month-old infants and to explore the sequential mediating roles of salivary oxytocin and mother-infant caregiving quality. The primary hypothesis is that higher PPF severity will correlate with poorer infant emotional development outcomes. The secondary hypothesis is that oxytocin levels and maternal caregiving sequentially mediate this association. METHODS: We will recruit 412 mother-infant dyads with maternal PPF within 1 week postpartum. PPF severity will be measured by the Postpartum Fatigue Scale. Infant emotional development, covering expression, regulation, and recognition, will be evaluated via questionnaires and physiological assessments, including eye-tracking and galvanic skin response, at an infant age of 3 months. papers.title: Evidence-based clinical practice national guideline for elective female genital aesthetic labiaplasty: recommendations from the pelvic floor and cosmetic gynecology (PETKOZ) association and expert consensus.
papers.journal: Journal of the Turkish German Gynecological Association
papers.abstract: The increasing global demand for elective female genital cosmetic surgery (FGCS), combined with substantial variability in clinical practice and patient counseling, highlights the need for standardized evidence-based guidance. This national guideline was developed by the Pelvic Floor and Cosmetic Gynecology Association to provide graded recommendations for the evaluation, surgical management, and perioperative care of women seeking elective FGCS, with particular emphasis on labiaplasty. A structured electronic database search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Scopus from inception through April 2026, supplemented by grey literature screening. Evidence grading followed the Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network classification. Methodological quality was appraised using AMSTAR 2, Cochrane RoB 2, and Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions. For clinical questions not sufficiently addressed by available literature, a three-round modified Delphi consensus process was conducted with 24 specialists, each with a minimum of 50 labiaplasty procedures. Of 1,514 records identified, 20 studies met inclusion criteria, comprising 8 systematic reviews and meta-analyses, 2 randomized controlled trials, and 10 observational cohort studies. Labiaplasty was associated with significant and reproducible postoperative improvements in genital self-image across all study designs, independent of surgical technique (grade B; evidence level 2+). Sexual function outcomes showed consistent improvement, predominantly in the pain and satisfaction domains, though overall certainty of evidence was very low owing to high heterogeneity and predominantly uncontrolled designs (grade C; evidence level 1-). papers.title: SEXUAL FUNCTION IN WOMEN UNDERGOING HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELL TRANSPLANTATION: RESULTS OF AN OBSERVATIONAL STUDY.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sexual health is a crucial component of human quality of life. Due to a combination of physical and psychological factors, women who undergo allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) are particularly vulnerable to sexual dysfunction. Nonetheless, sexual health remains under-inquired in this specific clinical context. OBJECTIVES: To assess the prevalence of sexual dysfunction in adult women in remission after allo-HSCT and explore correlations with clinical and psychological variables. METHODS: In this monocentric, cross-sectional study, women aged 18-65 in disease remission after allo-HSCT from 2012-2022 were enrolled. Anthropometric, clinical, biochemical, psychological, and socio-demographic data were collected during follow-up visits. Sexual function was evaluated using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) and the Female Sexual Distress Scale (FSDS). RESULTS: Forty-five women were enrolled, mean age was 48.3 years and the median time from transplant was 6.8 years. Sexual dysfunction was highly prevalent: 86% of patients had impaired FSFI scores, and 68.2% reported significant sexual distress on the FSDS. Psychological variables (anxiety, depression, distress, body image, relationship satisfaction) showed the strongest association with sexual dysfunction. Only specific sexual domains correlated with clinical factors (age, genital GvHD, secondary neoplasms). CONCLUSIONS: Sexual dysfunction was common in female allo-HSCT survivors, even years after transplantation, and was more strongly associated with psychological and relational factors than with disease- or treatment-related clinical variables. These observations highlight the need for a multidisciplinary approach, including sexual health into long-term survivorship care after HSCT.
